slides.title: Near-sensor Computing for Rapid Visuotactile Perception
slides.tldr: NEAR-SENSOR COMPUTING FOR FAST VISUOTACTILE PERCEPTION
slides.highlight: A near-sensor computing framework using a streaming hardware pipeline reduces latency and power consumption for tactile geometry reconstruction. This enables significantly faster robotic protective reflex loops compared to host-based processing.

card.one_liner: A near-sensor computing framework enables deterministic, ultra-low latency 3D visuotactile reconstruction for rapid robotic reflexes.
card.key_idea: A spectral Poisson solver implemented as a fully pipelined, non-iterative streaming hardware datapath on FPGA, providing fixed-latency depth reconstruction from raw pixel streams.
card.evaluation: Tested on 15 geometries (0.17% RMS error vs double-precision) and a protective reflex loop (28.3ms vs 169.9ms host-based). Results appear trustworthy.
card.limitation: Maximum supported grid size is currently limited by available on-chip memory for transform buffering.

slides.title: EvoHIL: Self-Evolving Reward and Flow-Matched Policy Optimization for Robust Human-in-the-Loop Reinforcement Learning
slides.highlight: EvoHIL improves robot manipulation through a framework that adapts reward models and stabilizes action generation, supporting the RwB goal of enhancing human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: EvoHIL improves robust human-in-the-loop RL via adaptive reward models, flow-matched action chunks, and visual adaptation.
card.key_idea: A staged framework combining self-evolving rewards (SER) from human feedback, flow-matching for temporally coherent action chunks (AFS), and retention-aware offline fine-tuning using relit interaction data.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on six manipulation tasks using Franka FR3 and SO-101 arms under lighting shifts; compared against HIL and imitation baselines.
card.limitation: Relies on an external relighter that may not reproduce all extreme illumination effects or preserve all task geometry.

slides.title: Semantic Haptic Feedback Enhances Dexterous Robotic Teleoperation
slides.tldr: ABSTRACT HAPTIC PATTERNS IMPROVE BIMANUAL TELEOPERATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces semantic haptics using abstract patterns to convey robot states, reducing hardware constraints and operator workload. It demonstrates superior performance in bimanual tasks compared to sensory haptics and visual feedback.

card.one_liner: Semantic haptic feedback using abstract patterns improves bimanual robotic teleoperation performance and reduces operator workload.
card.key_idea: Replaces high-fidelity sensory replication with symbolic haptic patterns (confirmations and exceptions) delivered via pneumatic and vibrotactile wristbands to communicate critical robot state transitions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via simulation (Box and Block/bimanual sorting tasks) against visual and sensory haptics. Semantic haptics showed superior bimanual performance and user preference.
card.limitation: The system was evaluated entirely within a simulation environment to simplify state estimation and haptic design testing.

slides.title: Variable Impedance Diffusion Policy for Compliant Robot Manipulation
slides.tldr: LEARNING VARIABLE IMPEDANCE CONTROL FROM KINEMATIC DEMONSTRATIONS
slides.highlight: This framework enables robots to predict both pose and task compliance from diverse demonstrations without requiring force sensors.

card.one_liner: VIDP learns variable impedance control from kinematic demonstrations to enable compliant, robust robot manipulation.
card.key_idea: Uses a Task-Parameterized Directionality-Aware Mixture Model (TP-DAMM) to extract trajectory distributions and map them to stiffness profiles for joint pose and compliance prediction.
card.evaluation: Real-world experiments compared VIDP against fixed-impedance baselines, measuring task success rate, interaction forces, and tracking errors.

slides.title: A Hierarchical Approach to Imitation Learning for Manipulation Tasks Requiring Time Varying Forces
slides.tldr: HIERARCHICAL DIFFUSION POLICY FOR HIGH-FREQUENCY FORCE REGULATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces DPA-FTG, which decouples low-frequency planning from high-frequency force regulation to enable stable contact in dynamic disassembly tasks.

card.one_liner: DPA-FTG enables high-frequency force regulation for contact-rich manipulation by decoupling low-frequency planning from high-frequency execution.
card.key_idea: A hierarchical architecture using a conditional diffusion model for slow task selection (5Hz) and a GRU-based neural impedance controller for fast, force-reactive trajectory generation (60Hz).
card.evaluation: Validated on a bimanual battery disassembly task (compliant sheet separation); outperformed state-of-the-art baselines, including Reactive Diffusion Policy (RDP).

slides.title: SiMDex: Mining Similar Egocentric Videos for Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Manipulation
slides.tldr: SIMILARITY-BASED EGOCENTRIC VIDEO MINING FOR DEXTEROUS MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: SiMDex uses a recall-ranking-re-ranking pipeline to extract task-relevant egocentric human samples for robot manipulation, supporting MOSAIC's focus on ego-exo views and skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: SiMDex improves dexterous manipulation by mining task-relevant human egocentric videos to augment VLA post-training.
card.key_idea: A three-layer recall–ranking–re-ranking pipeline retrieves similar human samples using a morphology-agnostic action space, treating data selection as a recommendation problem for VLA training.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on three real-world tasks (Drill, Flick Wheel, Pick & Place). Success rate rose from 47.7% to 61.1% versus random sampling.
card.limitation: Performance depends on human pool coverage; lacks contact force/object state data and is limited to a single industrial scenario.

slides.title: SpaceVLA: Spatially Grounded VLA for Robotic Manipulation with User-Authored Grasp and Place Anchors
slides.tldr: SPATIALLY GROUNDED VLA FOR ROBOTIC MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces Visual Intent Anchors to allow users to specify grasp and placement regions via XR overlays, improving spatial intent in VLA models.

card.one_liner: SpaceVLA uses user-authored visual anchors to guide VLA models for precise robotic pick-and-place manipulation.
card.key_idea: User-specified grasp and placement targets are rendered as color-coded image-space overlays on RGB observations, fine-tuning OpenVLA-7B via LoRA to follow these spatial cues.
card.evaluation: Evaluated in Unity on 80 held-out episodes; achieved 91.25% success rate with correct anchors, significantly outperforming no-anchor (50%) and random-anchor (77.5%) baselines.
card.limitation: Anchors are fixed image-space masks under a static camera and do not track moving objects or viewpoint changes.

slides.title: Textro: A Prototyping Toolkit for Solderless and Chipless Smart Textile Interfaces
slides.highlight: Textro introduces a toolkit for creating smart textile interfaces without rigid components or soldering, utilizing a web-based design environment and a wireless reader device.

card.one_liner: Textro is a toolkit for creating solderless, chipless smart textile interfaces using embroidery and capacitive coupling.
card.key_idea: It combines a web-based design environment, empirical models for textile RLC components, one-stroke embroidery paths, and glue-based capacitive coupling to eliminate rigid electronics and soldering.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via four application examples and a user study with 15 fashion experts, makers, and novices to assess usability.
